import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shephard's problem (a.k.a. Dürer's conjecture)

Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or simple edge-unfolding?

A (compact) convex polyhedron is the boundary of the convex hull $P$ of finitely many points of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ with nonempty interior. Cutting the boundary of $P$ along a spanning tree $T$ of the
edge graph of $P$ gives a surface $P_T$ (a disjoint union of the facets of $P$, glued back
together along the edges not in $T$). This surface is a topological disk that is locally
isometric to the plane, so it can be developed (unfolded) isometrically into $\mathbb{R}^2$.
Such an unfolding is called an *edge unfolding* of $P$. It is *simple* (or a *net*) when the
unfolding map $P_T \to \mathbb{R}^2$ is one-to-one, i.e. the unfolded faces do not overlap.

Shephard (1975) asked whether every convex polyhedron admits a simple edge unfolding. The
conjectured answer "yes" is known as Dürer's conjecture. The problem is open.

We follow the conventions of Ghomi (2014): "simple" means that the unfolding map is one-to-one,
so the images of two facets may only meet along an edge along which they are glued. The cut tree
must consist of genuine edges of $P$ (not pseudo-edges or subdivided faces).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Net (polyhedron)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shephard%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sh75] Shephard, G. C., *Convex polytopes with convex nets*, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.
  78 (1975), 389–403.
- [Gh14] Ghomi, M., *Affine unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Geom. Topol. 18 (2014), 3055–3090.
  [arXiv:1305.3231](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3231)
- [DO07] Demaine, E. D. and O'Rourke, J., *Geometric Folding Algorithms: Linkages, Origami,
  Polyhedra*, Cambridge University Press (2007), Chapter 22.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

/-- `IsFacet P F` means that `F` is a facet (a two-dimensional face) of the convex polytope
`P ⊆ ℝ³`: `F` is an exposed face of `P` whose affine span is a plane. -/
def IsFacet (P F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposed ℝ P F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ F) = 2

/-- The edge graph of the convex polytope `P ⊆ ℝ³`. Its vertices are the extreme points of `P`,
and two distinct vertices `v`, `w` are adjacent when the segment `[v, w]` is an (exposed) face of
`P`, i.e. an edge of `P`. -/
def edgeGraph (P : Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ) where
  Adj v w := v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ P (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w)
  symm v w h := ⟨h.1.symm, segment_symm ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ▸ h.2⟩
  loopless _ h := h.1 rfl

/-- A facet of `P` is nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma IsFacet.nonempty {P F : Set ℝ³} (hF : IsFacet P F) : F.Nonempty := by
  rw [Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
  rintro rfl
  have h := hF.2
  rw [vectorSpan_empty, finrank_bot] at h
  omega

/-- A facet of `P` is contained in `P`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma IsFacet.subset {P F : Set ℝ³} (hF : IsFacet P F) : F ⊆ P :=
  hF.1.subset

/-- A facet of a convex set `P` is convex. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma IsFacet.convex {P F : Set ℝ³} (hP : Convex ℝ P) (hF : IsFacet P F) : Convex ℝ F :=
  hF.1.convex hP

/-- Two vertices of `P` are adjacent in the edge graph iff they are distinct and the segment
between them is an exposed face of `P`. -/
@[simp, category API, AMS 52]
lemma edgeGraph_adj {P : Set ℝ³} (v w : P.extremePoints ℝ) :
    (edgeGraph P).Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ P (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w) :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The cut surface `P_T`, obtained by cutting the boundary of `P` along the spanning tree `T` of
its edge graph, is the disjoint union of the facets of `P` glued along the edges *not* in `T`.
A point of this disjoint union is a pair `(F, x)` with `F` a facet and `x ∈ F`.
`Glued P T (F, x) (G, y)` is the elementary gluing relation: `x = y` lies on an edge `[v, w]` of
`P` that is not cut (i.e. `v`, `w` are not adjacent in `T`) and is contained in both facets `F` and
`G`. The cut surface `P_T` is the quotient of the disjoint union of the facets by the equivalence
relation generated by `Glued P T`. -/
def Glued (P : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ)) :
    Set ℝ³ × ℝ³ → Set ℝ³ × ℝ³ → Prop :=
  fun a b => IsFacet P a.1 ∧ IsFacet P b.1 ∧ a.2 = b.2 ∧
    ∃ v w : P.extremePoints ℝ, (edgeGraph P).Adj v w ∧ ¬ T.Adj v w ∧
      segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ a.1 ∩ b.1 ∧ a.2 ∈ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w

/-- Glued facet-points are copies of the same point of `P`. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma Glued.snd_eq {P : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ)} {a b : Set ℝ³ × ℝ³}
    (h : Glued P T a b) : a.2 = b.2 :=
  h.2.2.1

/-- The gluing relation is symmetric. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
lemma Glued.symm {P : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ)} {a b : Set ℝ³ × ℝ³}
    (h : Glued P T a b) : Glued P T b a := by
  obtain ⟨ha, hb, hab, v, w, hvw, hT, hsub, hmem⟩ := h
  exact ⟨hb, ha, hab.symm, v, w, hvw, hT, Set.inter_comm _ _ ▸ hsub, hab ▸ hmem⟩

/-- `IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding P T φ` means that `φ` is a simple (one-to-one) unfolding of the boundary
of the convex polytope `P ⊆ ℝ³` cut along the spanning tree `T` of its edge graph. Here `φ F x`
is the position in the plane `ℝ²` of the point `x` of the facet `F` (the value of `φ F` off `F`,
and for `F` not a facet, is irrelevant). The conditions are:
- each facet is placed isometrically in the plane;
- two facets sharing an uncut edge are placed so that they agree along that edge, so that `φ`
  induces a map from the cut surface `P_T` to `ℝ²`;
- this induced map `P_T → ℝ²` is one-to-one: if the images of two facet-points coincide, then
  they are the same point of `P_T`. -/
def IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (P : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ))
    (φ : Set ℝ³ → ℝ³ → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  (∀ F, IsFacet P F → ∀ x ∈ F, ∀ y ∈ F, dist (φ F x) (φ F y) = dist x y) ∧
  (∀ F x G y, Glued P T (F, x) (G, y) → φ F x = φ G y) ∧
  (∀ F G, IsFacet P F → IsFacet P G → ∀ x ∈ F, ∀ y ∈ G,
    φ F x = φ G y → Relation.EqvGen (Glued P T) (F, x) (G, y))

/-- The convex polytope `P ⊆ ℝ³` has a net (a simple edge unfolding): there is a spanning tree
`T` of the edge graph of `P` such that cutting the boundary of `P` along `T` and unfolding it
isometrically into the plane gives a one-to-one map. -/
def HasNet (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ), T ≤ edgeGraph P ∧ T.IsTree ∧
    ∃ φ : Set ℝ³ → ℝ³ → ℝ², IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding P T φ

/-- **Shephard's problem (Dürer's conjecture).** Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or
simple edge-unfolding? That is, for every finite set of points of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose convex hull
$P$ has nonempty interior, is there a spanning tree $T$ of the edge graph of $P$ such that cutting
the boundary of $P$ along $T$ and developing it isometrically into the plane is one-to-one? -/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem shephards_problem_a_k_a_durers_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ S : Finset ℝ³, (interior (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ³))).Nonempty →
      HasNet (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ³)) := by
  sorry

end ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

modeling_decisions: Convex polyhedron = boundary of `convexHull ℝ S` for a `Finset ℝ³` with nonempty interior (Ghomi's definition, as in the decomposition notes and the repo's Rupert.lean idiom); the theorem quantifies over all such `S`.

Vertices are `Set.extremePoints ℝ P`; edges are segments `[v,w]` (v ≠ w) with `IsExposed ℝ P (segment ℝ v w)`; facets are exposed subsets whose `vectorSpan` has finrank 2. For a polytope, exposed subsets are exactly the faces, so these are exactly the vertices, edges and 2-faces. The definitions are only meaningful for polytopes; they are applied only to `convexHull ℝ S`.

A spanning tree of the edge graph is `T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ)` with `T ≤ edgeGraph P` and `T.IsTree` (a tree on the whole vertex type is automatically spanning). The cut tree therefore consists of genuine edges only (no pseudo-edges, no face subdivisions).

An edge unfolding is encoded facet-by-facet: `φ : Set ℝ³ → ℝ³ → ℝ²`, `φ F x` = planar position of the point `x` of facet `F`; values off `F` or for non-facets `F` are irrelevant junk. Condition 1: `φ F` is distance-preserving on each facet (so the image is a congruent copy of the facet). Condition 2: for facets `F`, `G` sharing an uncut edge, `φ F = φ G` on that edge (so `φ` descends to the cut surface `P_T`). Condition 3 (simplicity): `φ F x = φ G y → Relation.EqvGen (Glued P T) (F, x) (G, y)`, i.e. the induced map `P_T → ℝ²` is injective.

'Simple'/'non-overlapping' is taken in Ghomi's one-to-one sense (the unfolding map on the cut surface is injective; touching along cut edges or at unglued vertex copies is not allowed), following the decomposition notes and Demaine–O'Rourke's 'simple polygon' convention. The weaker 'interiors of faces pairwise disjoint' reading was not used.

Ghomi's orientation-preserving requirement is omitted: with the gluing condition, placing a facet on the wrong side of a glued edge forces an interior overlap, which injectivity (condition 3) forbids, and a global reflection of a one-to-one unfolding is again one-to-one. Hence `HasNet` is equivalent to the existence of a simple edge unfolding in Ghomi's sense.
`Glued` requires both components to be facets, so `EqvGen` chains cannot pass through junk (non-facet) sets and identify points that are not identified in `P_T`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shephard's problem (a.k.a. Dürer's conjecture)

Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or simple edge-unfolding?

A (compact) convex polyhedron is the boundary of the convex hull of finitely many points of
$\mathbb{R}^3$ which do not all lie in a plane. An *edge unfolding* is obtained by cutting the
surface along a spanning tree of its edge graph and developing the resulting surface isometrically
into the plane. The unfolding is *simple* (a *net*) if the development is one-to-one, i.e. the
unfolded faces do not overlap.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Net (polyhedron)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shephard%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Sh75] Shephard, G. C., _Convex polytopes with convex nets_. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.
  78 (1975), 389–403.
- [Gh14] Ghomi, M., _Affine unfoldings of convex polyhedra_. Geom. Topol. 18 (2014), 3055–3090.
  [arXiv:1305.3231](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3231)
- [BG19] Barvinok, N., Ghomi, M., _Pseudo-edge unfoldings of convex polyhedra_. Discrete Comput.
  Geom. 64 (2020), 671–689. [arXiv:1709.04944](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.04944)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

/--
`IsFacet K F` means that `F` is a facet (a two-dimensional face) of the convex polytope
`K ⊆ ℝ³`: `F` is an exposed face of `K` (the set of maximisers over `K` of some linear
functional) which lies in a plane but not in a line.
-/
def IsFacet (K F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposed ℝ K F ∧ Coplanar ℝ F ∧ ¬ Collinear ℝ F

/-- The type of facets of the convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³`. -/
abbrev Facet (K : Set ℝ³) : Type := {F : Set ℝ³ // IsFacet K F}

/--
The edge graph of the convex polytope `K ⊆ ℝ³`. Its vertices are the extreme points of `K`, and
two distinct vertices are adjacent if and only if the segment joining them is an exposed face of
`K`, i.e. an edge of `K`.
-/
def edgeGraph (K : Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ) where
  Adj v w := v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w)
  symm v w h := ⟨h.1.symm, segment_symm ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ▸ h.2⟩
  loopless _ h := h.1 rfl

/--
Cutting the surface of the convex polytope `K` along the subgraph `T` of its edge graph.
A point of the cut surface is represented by a pair `(F, x)` where `F` is a facet of `K` and
`x ∈ F`. Two such pairs `(F, x)` and `(F', x')` are *directly glued* if `x = x'` lies on an edge
of `K` which is contained in both `F` and `F'` and which is **not** cut, i.e. is not an edge of
`T`. The points of the cut surface are the equivalence classes of the equivalence relation
`Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T)` generated by this relation.
-/
def Glued (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) (p q : Facet K × ℝ³) : Prop :=
  p.2 = q.2 ∧ ∃ v w, (edgeGraph K).Adj v w ∧ ¬ T.Adj v w ∧
    segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ p.1.1 ∧ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ q.1.1 ∧
    p.2 ∈ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w

/--
`IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding K T u` means that `u` is a simple (one-to-one) unfolding of the surface of
the convex polytope `K` cut along the subgraph `T` of its edge graph. Here `u F x ∈ ℝ²` is the
position, after unfolding, of the point `x` of the facet `F`:
* each facet is moved rigidly (distances between points of a facet are preserved),
* points identified in the cut surface (see `Glued`) go to the same point of the plane,
* distinct points of the cut surface go to distinct points of the plane, so that the unfolded
  facets do not overlap.
-/
structure IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (K : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ))
    (u : Facet K → ℝ³ → ℝ²) : Prop where
  dist_eq : ∀ (F : Facet K), ∀ x ∈ F.1, ∀ y ∈ F.1, dist (u F x) (u F y) = dist x y
  glue : ∀ p q, Glued K T p q → u p.1 p.2 = u q.1 q.2
  injective : ∀ (F F' : Facet K), ∀ x ∈ F.1, ∀ y ∈ F'.1,
    u F x = u F' y → Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T) (F, x) (F', y)

/-- The empty set is not a facet. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem not_isFacet_empty (K : Set ℝ³) : ¬ IsFacet K ∅ :=
  fun h => h.2.2 (collinear_empty ℝ ℝ³)

/-- Glued points of the cut surface are the same point of the polytope. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem Glued.snd_eq {K : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)}
    {p q : Facet K × ℝ³} (h : Glued K T p q) : p.2 = q.2 :=
  h.1

/-- Points identified in the cut surface are copies of the same point of the polytope. -/
@[category API, AMS 52]
theorem eqvGen_glued_snd_eq {K : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)}
    {p q : Facet K × ℝ³} (h : Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T) p q) : p.2 = q.2 := by
  induction h with
  | rel _ _ h => exact h.snd_eq
  | refl _ => rfl
  | symm _ _ _ ih => exact ih.symm
  | trans _ _ _ _ _ ih₁ ih₂ => exact ih₁.trans ih₂

/--
**Shephard's problem (Dürer's conjecture).**
Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or simple edge-unfolding?

Precisely: for every finite set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ of points not all lying in a plane, is
there a spanning tree $T$ of the edge graph of the convex polytope $K = \operatorname{conv}(S)$
such that the surface of $K$ cut along $T$ admits a one-to-one isometric unfolding into the plane
$\mathbb{R}^2$? The conjectured answer is *yes*.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem shephards_problem_a_k_a_durers_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ S : Finset ℝ³, ¬ Coplanar ℝ (S : Set ℝ³) →
      ∃ T ≤ edgeGraph (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ³)), T.IsTree ∧
        ∃ u, IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ³)) T u := by
  sorry

end ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot table matches the statement; 'net' and 'simple edge-unfolding' are treated as synonyms as the notes prescribe.
modeling_decisions: Convex polyhedron = boundary of convexHull ℝ S for a finite S ⊆ ℝ³ with ¬ Coplanar ℝ S (points not all in a plane, as in Barvinok–Ghomi), i.e. a genuine 3-dimensional polytope; the surface is modelled as the union of facets (exposed faces of dimension 2).

Edges are exposed 1-faces of the polytope (segments between two extreme points that are exposed sets); the cut tree T is a SimpleGraph on the extreme points with T ≤ edgeGraph and T.IsTree, i.e. a spanning tree of actual edges only (no pseudo-edges, no face subdivision).

Non-overlap follows Ghomi's 'one-to-one' convention: the induced map on the cut surface P_T is injective. In particular two copies of a vertex lying in different sectors (separated by cut edges) must map to distinct points, and boundary touching of the unfolded polygons is not allowed. The alternative 'disjoint interiors' convention would be weaker; the one named in the decomposition notes was chosen.

The unfolding is encoded per facet (u : Facet K → ℝ³ → ℝ², only values on the facet matter) with distance preservation within facets, agreement on glued points, and injectivity modulo Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T). This is equivalent to an injective isometric immersion of P_T: injectivity forces facets adjacent along an uncut edge to lie on opposite sides of its image, so the development is locally isometric and consistently oriented; orientation-reversing (mirror) developments are allowed, which is harmless for existence.
The question form of the Wikipedia entry is kept via `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`; answer(True) is the conjectured positive answer.

def IsConvexPolyhedron (P : Finset ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ConvexIndependent ℝ ((↑) : ↥(P : Set ℝ³) → ℝ³) ∧ affineSpan ℝ (P : Set ℝ³) = ⊤

/-- `F` is the set of vertices on a proper exposed face of the polytope with vertices `P`. -/
def IsExposedFace (P F : Finset ℝ³) : Prop :=
  F ⊆ P ∧ ∃ f : ℝ³ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ, f ≠ 0 ∧ ∃ c : ℝ,
    (∀ p ∈ P, f p ≤ c) ∧ ∀ p, p ∈ F ↔ p ∈ P ∧ f p = c

/-- `F` is the vertex set of a two-dimensional facet of the polytope with vertices `P`. -/
def IsFacet (P F : Finset ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposedFace P F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ (F : Set ℝ³)).direction = 2

/-- `E` is the vertex set of an actual one-dimensional edge of the polytope with vertices `P`. -/
def IsEdge (P E : Finset ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposedFace P E ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ (E : Set ℝ³)).direction = 1

/-- The graph whose vertices and edges are the actual vertices and edges of the polytope. -/
def edgeGraph (P : Finset ℝ³) : SimpleGraph ↥P :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun p q ↦ IsEdge P {p.1, q.1}

/-- A point in a labelled copy of one of the closed facets of the polytope. -/
def FacetPoint (P : Finset ℝ³) :=
  Σ F : {F : Finset ℝ³ // IsFacet P F},

actual edge shared by their two facets. -/
def GluedAlongUncutEdge (P : Finset ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph ↥P)
    (z w : FacetPoint P) : Prop :=
  z.2.1 = w.2.1 ∧ ∃ p q : ↥P,
    p ≠ q ∧ IsEdge P {p.1, q.1} ∧ ¬T.Adj p q ∧

/-!
# Shephard's problem (a.k.a. Dürer's conjecture)

Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or simple edge-unfolding?

A *convex polyhedron* is the boundary of the convex hull `P` of finitely many points of `ℝ³`
that do not all lie in a plane (equivalently, `P` has nonempty interior). Its faces, edges and
vertices are the two-, one- and zero-dimensional faces of the polytope `P`. An *edge unfolding*
of `P` is obtained by cutting the surface along a spanning tree `T` of the edge graph of `P`
(so the cuts run along actual edges only, and every vertex is reached by a cut); the cut surface
is a topological disk that is locally isometric to the plane, so it can be developed isometrically
(face by face, keeping the faces intact) into `ℝ²`. The unfolding is *simple*, and its image is a
*net*, if this development is one-to-one, i.e. the faces do not overlap in the plane.

Shephard (1975) asked whether every convex polyhedron admits a simple edge unfolding, and the
conjectured positive answer is known as Dürer's conjecture. The question remains open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Net (polyhedron)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shephard%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- G. C. Shephard, *Convex polytopes with convex nets*, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 78
  (1975), 389–403.
- M. Ghomi, *Affine unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Geom. Topol. 18 (2014), 3055–3090,
  [arXiv:1305.3231](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3231).
- N. Barvinok, M. Ghomi, *Pseudo-edge unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Discrete Comput. Geom.
  64 (2020), 671–689, [arXiv:1709.04944](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.04944).
-/

namespace ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

/-- The edge graph of a convex polytope `P ⊆ ℝ³`. Its vertices are the extreme points of `P`,
and two distinct vertices `v`, `w` are adjacent if the segment `[v, w]` is a face of `P`
(an exposed subset of `P`), i.e. if `[v, w]` is an edge of `P`. -/
def edgeGraph (P : Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ) where
  Adj v w := v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ P (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w)
  symm v w := by
    rintro ⟨hne, hexp⟩
    exact ⟨hne.symm, segment_symm ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ▸ hexp⟩
  loopless v := by
    rintro ⟨hne, -⟩
    exact hne rfl

/-- The faces of a convex polytope `P ⊆ ℝ³`: the exposed subsets of `P` whose affine span is a
plane, i.e. the two-dimensional faces (the polygons making up the boundary of `P`). -/
abbrev Face (P : Set ℝ³) : Type :=
  {F : Set ℝ³ // IsExposed ℝ P F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ F) = 2}

/-- Cutting the boundary of `P` along a subgraph `T` of its edge graph. A point `x` of a face `F`
and a point `y` of a face `F'` are directly glued if `x = y` lies on a common edge `[v, w]` of
`F` and `F'` that is *not* cut, i.e. `v w` is an edge of `P` but not an edge of `T`. The cut
surface `P_T` is the quotient of the disjoint union of the faces of `P` by the equivalence
relation generated by this relation (see `Relation.EqvGen`). -/
def GluedAlong (P : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ)) :
    Face P × ℝ³ → Face P × ℝ³ → Prop :=
  fun p q => p.2 = q.2 ∧ ∃ v w : P.extremePoints ℝ, (edgeGraph P).Adj v w ∧ ¬ T.Adj v w ∧
    segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ p.1.1 ∧ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ q.1.1 ∧ p.2 ∈ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w

/-- `f` is a simple (one-to-one) unfolding of the boundary of `P` cut along `T`: the map
`f F : ℝ³ → ℝ²` develops each face `F` of `P` isometrically into the plane, points identified in
the cut surface `P_T` are sent to the same point (so `f` is a continuous, face-wise isometric map
`P_T → ℝ²`), and the induced map `P_T → ℝ²` is injective, i.e. two points of faces with the same
image in the plane are the same point of the cut surface `P_T`. -/
def IsSimpleUnfolding (P : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ))
    (f : Face P → ℝ³ → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  (∀ F : Face P, ∀ x ∈ F.1, ∀ y ∈ F.1, dist (f F x) (f F y) = dist x y) ∧
  (∀ p q, GluedAlong P T p q → f p.1 p.2 = f q.1 q.2) ∧
  (∀ (F F' : Face P), ∀ x ∈ F.1, ∀ y ∈ F'.1, f F x = f F' y →
    Relation.EqvGen (GluedAlong P T) (F, x) (F', y))

/-- A convex polytope `P ⊆ ℝ³` has a *net*, or *simple edge unfolding*, if there is a spanning
tree `T` of its edge graph such that cutting the boundary of `P` along `T` and developing it
isometrically into the plane is one-to-one. -/
def HasNet (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ), T ≤ edgeGraph P ∧ T.IsTree ∧
    ∃ f : Face P → ℝ³ → ℝ², IsSimpleUnfolding P T f

/-- The direct gluing relation is symmetric. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem gluedAlong_symm {P : Set ℝ³} {T : SimpleGraph (P.extremePoints ℝ)} {p q : Face P × ℝ³}
    (h : GluedAlong P T p q) : GluedAlong P T q p := by
  obtain ⟨hpq, v, w, hvw, hT, hp, hq, hx⟩ := h
  exact ⟨hpq.symm, v, w, hvw, hT, hq, hp, hpq ▸ hx⟩

/-- **Shephard's problem (Dürer's conjecture).** Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or
simple edge-unfolding? That is, for every convex polyhedron, the boundary of the convex hull `P`
of a finite set of points of `ℝ³` with nonempty interior, is there a spanning tree `T` of the edge
graph of `P` such that cutting the boundary of `P` along `T` and developing it isometrically into
the plane `ℝ²` is one-to-one (the faces do not overlap)? The conjectured answer is yes. -/

    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ S : Finset ℝ³, (interior (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ³))).Nonempty →
      HasNet (convexHull ℝ (S : Set ℝ³)) := by

end ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

/-- A facet of a three-dimensional polytope is a two-dimensional exposed face. -/
def IsFacet (P F : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsExposed ℝ P F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ F).direction = 2

/-- The facets of a polytope, represented by their point sets. -/
abbrev Facet (P : Set ℝ³) := {F : Set ℝ³ // IsFacet P F}

/-- The vertices of a polytope are its extreme points. -/
abbrev PolytopeVertex (P : Set ℝ³) := P.extremePoints ℝ

/--
The actual edge graph of a polytope. Two distinct vertices are adjacent exactly when their closed
segment is an exposed face of the polytope.
-/
def edgeGraph (P : Set ℝ³) : SimpleGraph (PolytopeVertex P) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun u v ↦ IsExposed ℝ P (segment ℝ (u : ℝ³) (v : ℝ³))

/-- A point of the disjoint union of all facets of a polytope. -/
abbrev FacePoint (P : Set ℝ³) := Σ F : Facet P, F.1

/--
Two copies of a surface point are directly glued after cutting along `T` when they lie in facets
sharing an actual edge which is not in `T`.
-/
def GluedAcrossUncutEdge (P : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (PolytopeVertex P))
    (p q : FacePoint P) : Prop :=
  (p.2 : ℝ³) = (q.2 : ℝ³) ∧
    ∃ v w : PolytopeVertex P,
      (edgeGraph P).Adj v w ∧ ¬T.Adj v w ∧
      (p.2 : ℝ³) ∈ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) (w : ℝ³) ∧
      segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) (w : ℝ³) ⊆ p.1.1 ∧
      segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) (w : ℝ³) ⊆ q.1.1

/--
`T` gives a simple edge-unfolding of `P` if it is a spanning tree of the actual edge graph and the
facets admit distance-preserving planar developments which agree exactly on points identified in
the cut surface. The reverse implication in the final equivalence excludes all other overlaps,
including accidental contacts between distinct boundary points.
-/
def IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (P : Set ℝ³) (T : SimpleGraph (PolytopeVertex P)) : Prop :=
  T ≤ edgeGraph P ∧ T.IsTree ∧
    ∃ develop : ∀ F : Facet P, F.1 → ℝ²,
      (∀ (F : Facet P) (x y : F.1),
        dist (develop F x) (develop F y) = dist (x : ℝ³) (y : ℝ³)) ∧
      ∀ p q : FacePoint P,
        develop p.1 p.2 = develop q.1 q.2 ↔
          Relation.EqvGen (GluedAcrossUncutEdge P T) p q

/--
**Shephard's problem (Dürer's conjecture).** Does every compact convex polyhedron in
$\mathbb{R}^3$ have a net (equivalently, a simple edge-unfolding)? Precisely: for every convex
hull of finitely many points with nonempty interior, is there a spanning tree consisting only of
actual polyhedron edges such that cutting the boundary along that tree admits a facewise
isometric, one-to-one development into $\mathbb{R}^2$? Here one-to-one means that two developed
points coincide exactly when their face copies are identified across uncut edges, so distinct
boundary points are not allowed merely to touch.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem shephards_problem_a_k_a_durers_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ vertices : Finset ℝ³,
        (interior (convexHull ℝ (vertices : Set ℝ³))).Nonempty →
          let P := convexHull ℝ (vertices : Set ℝ³)
          ∃ T : SimpleGraph (PolytopeVertex P), IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding P T := by
  sorry

end ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

Shephard's problem asks whether the boundary of every three-dimensional compact convex polytope
can be cut along a spanning tree of its actual edges and developed into the plane without overlap.
Here “without overlap” means that the development of the cut surface is one-to-one, including on
its boundary.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Shephard's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shephard%27s_conjecture)
- [Barvinok and Ghomi, *Pseudo-edge unfoldings of convex polyhedra*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.04944)

namespace ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

abbrev Point3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
abbrev Point2 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- A facet of a full-dimensional convex polytope `K` is a two-dimensional exposed face of `K`. -/
def Facet (K : Set Point3) :=
  {F : Set Point3 // IsExposed ℝ K F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ F).direction = 2}

/-- The actual edge graph of `K`. Its vertices are the extreme points of `K`, and two distinct
vertices are adjacent exactly when their line segment is an exposed face of `K`. -/
def edgeGraph (K : Set Point3) : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun v w => IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ (v : Point3) (w : Point3))

/-- A point in a labelled facet, before common uncut edges are identified. -/
def FacePoint (K : Set Point3) := Σ F : Facet K, F.1

/-- Two labelled face points are directly glued when they are the same spatial point on an actual
edge which is not in the cut tree, and both of their facets contain that edge. -/
def DirectlyGlued (K : Set Point3) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ))
    (x y : FacePoint K) : Prop :=
  (x.2 : Point3) = (y.2 : Point3) ∧
    ∃ v w, (edgeGraph K).Adj v w ∧ ¬ T.Adj v w ∧
      segment ℝ (v : Point3) (w : Point3) ⊆ x.1.1 ∧
      segment ℝ (v : Point3) (w : Point3) ⊆ y.1.1 ∧
      (x.2 : Point3) ∈ segment ℝ (v : Point3) (w : Point3)

/-- The boundary of `K` cut along `T`: the disjoint union of all facets, with the copies of each
actual edge outside `T` glued together. The equivalence closure also makes the correct
identifications among copies of vertices. -/
def CutSurface (K : Set Point3) (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) :=
  Quotient (Relation.EqvGen.setoid (DirectlyGlued K T))

/-- `K` has a simple edge-unfolding if some spanning tree of its actual edge graph cuts its
boundary into a surface admitting an injective facewise isometric development into the plane.
Injectivity is imposed on the entire cut surface, so distinct boundary points may not touch. -/
def HasSimpleEdgeUnfolding (K : Set Point3) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ), T ≤ edgeGraph K ∧ T.IsTree ∧
    ∃ u : CutSurface K T → Point2, Function.Injective u ∧
      ∀ (F : Facet K) (x y : F.1),
        dist (u (Quotient.mk _ ⟨F, x⟩)) (u (Quotient.mk _ ⟨F, y⟩)) =
          dist (x : Point3) (y : Point3)

/--
**Shephard's problem (Dürer's conjecture).** Does every compact convex polyhedron in
$\mathbb{R}^3$ have a net, or simple edge-unfolding? Precisely, is it true that for every convex
hull of finitely many points with nonempty interior, there is a spanning tree of the polyhedron's
actual edge graph such that cutting its boundary along that tree admits a one-to-one facewise
isometric development into $\mathbb{R}^2$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem shephards_problem_a_k_a_durers_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ V : Finset Point3,
      (interior (convexHull ℝ (V : Set Point3))).Nonempty →
        HasSimpleEdgeUnfolding (convexHull ℝ (V : Set Point3)) := by
  sorry

end ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

Facets are modeled as the two-dimensional exposed faces of the solid convex hull. For a finite-dimensional polytope these are exactly its polygonal facets.

Vertices are the extreme points of the convex hull, and actual edges are exactly the nondegenerate segments between such vertices that are exposed faces. This excludes pseudo-edges, geodesic diagonals, and face subdivisions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shephard's problem (a.k.a. Dürer's conjecture)

Does every convex polyhedron have a net, or simple edge-unfolding?

A convex polyhedron is the boundary of the convex hull of finitely many points of $\mathbb{R}^3$
with nonempty interior. Cutting it along a spanning tree $T$ of its edge graph yields a surface
$P_T$ (a topological disk) which can be developed isometrically into the plane. This development
is a *simple edge unfolding*, or *net*, if it is one-to-one (non-overlapping). Shephard's problem
asks whether every convex polyhedron admits such a spanning tree; the conjectured answer is yes.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Net (polyhedron)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shephard%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- G. C. Shephard, *Convex polytopes with convex nets*, Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 78
  (1975), 389–403.
- M. Ghomi, *Affine unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Geom. Topol. 18 (2014), 3055–3090.
  [arXiv:1305.3231](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3231)
- N. Barvinok, M. Ghomi, *Pseudo-edge unfoldings of convex polyhedra*, Discrete Comput. Geom.
  64 (2020), 671–689. [arXiv:1709.04944](https://arxiv.org/abs/1709.04944)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

variable (K : Set ℝ³)

/--
The edge graph of a convex polyhedron $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$. Its vertices are the extreme
points (vertices) of $K$, and two vertices are adjacent when the segment joining them is an exposed
face of $K$, i.e. an edge of $K$.
-/
def edgeGraph : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ) where
  Adj v w := v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w)
  symm v w h := ⟨h.1.symm, segment_symm ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ▸ h.2⟩
  loopless _ h := h.1 rfl

/-- The (two-dimensional) faces of a convex polyhedron $K$: its exposed faces of dimension two. -/
def faces : Set (Set ℝ³) :=
  {F | IsExposed ℝ K F ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ F) = 2}

/--
The one-step gluing relation on the disjoint union of the faces of $K$ after cutting along the
tree $T$ of edges: a point $x$ of a face $F$ is glued to the same point $x$ of a face $F'$ when
$x$ lies on an edge of $K$ which is contained in both $F$ and $F'$ and is not cut, i.e. is not an
edge of $T$. The surface $K_T$ obtained by cutting $K$ along $T$ is the quotient of the disjoint
union of the faces by the equivalence relation generated by this relation.
-/
def Glued (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)) (p q : ℝ³ × faces K) : Prop :=
  p.1 = q.1 ∧ ∃ v w, (edgeGraph K).Adj v w ∧ ¬ T.Adj v w ∧
    p.1 ∈ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ∧ segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w ⊆ (p.2 : Set ℝ³) ∩ q.2

/--
`IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding K T f` says that the maps `f F : ℝ³ → ℝ²`, one for each face `F` of `K`,
constitute a simple (one-to-one) unfolding of `K` cut along the edge tree `T`:
* each `f F` is an isometry on the face `F`, i.e. `f F` develops `F` in the plane;
* two faces glued along an uncut edge are developed consistently along that edge, so that the
  `f F` assemble into a map $u : K_T \to \mathbb{R}^2$ on the cut surface;
* the resulting map $u$ is one-to-one: whenever two points of faces have the same image, they are
  the same point of $K_T$, i.e. they are identified by the gluing.
-/
structure IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ))
    (f : faces K → ℝ³ → ℝ²) : Prop where
  dist_eq : ∀ (F : faces K), ∀ x ∈ (F : Set ℝ³), ∀ y ∈ (F : Set ℝ³),
    dist (f F x) (f F y) = dist x y
  glue : ∀ p q, Glued K T p q → f p.2 p.1 = f q.2 q.1
  injective : ∀ (F F' : faces K), ∀ x ∈ (F : Set ℝ³), ∀ y ∈ (F' : Set ℝ³),
    f F x = f F' y → Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T) (x, F) (y, F')

/--
A convex polyhedron $K$ *has a net* (or a *simple edge-unfolding*) if there is a spanning tree
$T$ of its edge graph such that cutting $K$ along $T$ and developing the result isometrically into
the plane gives a one-to-one (non-overlapping) map.
-/
def HasNet : Prop :=
  ∃ T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ), T ≤ edgeGraph K ∧ T.IsTree ∧
    ∃ f : faces K → ℝ³ → ℝ², IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding K T f

    (edgeGraph K).Adj v w ↔ v ≠ w ∧ IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ (v : ℝ³) w) :=
  Iff.rfl

theorem Glued.symm {T : SimpleGraph (K.extremePoints ℝ)} {p q : ℝ³ × faces K}

  obtain ⟨hpq, v, w, hvw, hT, hp, hsub⟩ := h
  exact ⟨hpq.symm, v, w, hvw, hT, hpq ▸ hp, Set.inter_comm _ _ ▸ hsub⟩

/--

edge-unfolding? That is, given the boundary of the convex hull $K$ of finitely many points of

$\mathbb{R}^2$ is one-to-one (the faces do not overlap)? The conjectured answer is yes.
-/

    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ S : Finset ℝ³,

end ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

Vertices are `K.extremePoints ℝ`; an edge is a segment between two distinct vertices that is an exposed face of K (`IsExposed ℝ K (segment ℝ v w)`); a face is an exposed face F with `Module.finrank ℝ (vectorSpan ℝ F) = 2`. A cut tree is a `SimpleGraph T` on the vertex type `K.extremePoints ℝ` with `T ≤ edgeGraph K` and `T.IsTree`; since `IsTree` requires connectivity on the whole vertex type, T is automatically spanning. The cut surface K_T is not built as a topological space. Instead an unfolding is a family `f : faces K → ℝ³ → ℝ²` with (i) each `f F` distance-preserving on F, (ii) `f F x = f F' x` whenever the point x of F is glued to the point x of F' (x lies on an uncut edge contained in F ∩ F'), and (iii) one-to-one: `f F x = f F' y` implies `(x,F)` and `(y,F')` are related by `Relation.EqvGen (Glued K T)`, i.e. they are the same point of K_T. This is Barvinok–Ghomi's 'isometric immersion of K_T which is one-to-one'.

Non-overlap is taken in Ghomi's 'one-to-one' sense: two faces whose developments merely touch along boundary points not identified by the gluing count as overlapping. This convention is applied uniformly.

Orientation-preservation of the unfolding (Ghomi's convention) is not imposed: injectivity forces glued faces to lie on opposite sides of their common edge, so any injective family is either everywhere orientation-preserving or everywhere orientation-reversing, and reflecting ℝ² converts one to the other. Existence is therefore unaffected.

The question is stated in `answer(sorry) ↔ ...` form: `answer(True)` is the conjectured positive answer (every convex polyhedron has a net); `answer(False)` would mean some convex polyhedron has no net.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Shephard's problem (Dürer's conjecture)

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Shephard's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shephard%27s_conjecture)
-/

namespace ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture

private abbrev Space := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
private abbrev Plane := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)

/-- An exposed face `F` of `P` whose affine span has dimension `d`. -/
private def IsExposedFaceOfDim (P F : Set Space) (d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  F.Nonempty ∧
    ∃ (l : Space →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (a : ℝ), l ≠ 0 ∧
      (∀ x ∈ P, l x ≤ a) ∧
      F = {x ∈ P | l x = a} ∧
      Module.finrank ℝ (affineSpan ℝ F).direction = d

/-- The actual (one-dimensional) edges of a convex polytope. -/
private def IsEdge (P e : Set Space) : Prop :=
  IsExposedFaceOfDim P e 1

/-- The polygonal (two-dimensional) facets of a convex three-dimensional polytope. -/
private abbrev Facet (P : Set Space) :=
  {F : Set Space // IsExposedFaceOfDim P F 2}

/-- The vertices of a convex polytope. -/
private abbrev Vertex (P : Set Space) :=
  P.extremePoints ℝ

/-- The edge graph of a convex polytope, with adjacency given only by actual edges. -/
private def edgeGraph (P : Set Space) : SimpleGraph (Vertex P) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel fun u v ↦ IsEdge P (segment ℝ (u : Space) v)

/-- A point in a labelled facet. Distinct copies are retained until uncut edges are glued. -/
private abbrev FacetPoint (P : Set Space) :=
  Σ F : Facet P, F

/-- An edge is cut when it is the segment belonging to an edge of the chosen tree. -/
private def IsCutEdge (P : Set Space) (T : SimpleGraph (Vertex P)) (e : Set Space) : Prop :=
  ∃ u v, T.Adj u v ∧ e = segment ℝ (u : Space) v

/--
The elementary gluing relation on labelled facets after cutting along `T`: copies of the same
spatial point are glued across an actual edge precisely when that edge is not in `T`.
-/
private def GluedAcrossUncutEdge (P : Set Space) (T : SimpleGraph (Vertex P))
    (p q : FacetPoint P) : Prop :=
  (p.2 : Space) = q.2 ∧
    ∃ e : Set Space, IsEdge P e ∧ ¬ IsCutEdge P T e ∧
      e ⊆ (p.1 : Set Space) ∧ e ⊆ (q.1 : Set Space) ∧ (p.2 : Space) ∈ e

/--
`T` gives a simple edge-unfolding when it is a spanning tree made of actual edges and the cut
surface has a one-to-one planar development that preserves Euclidean distances on every facet.
The equivalence closure describes exactly the identifications left across uncut edges; the final
biconditional excludes all additional intersections, including incidental boundary contacts.
-/
private def IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (P : Set Space) (T : SimpleGraph (Vertex P)) : Prop :=
  T ≤ edgeGraph P ∧ T.Connected ∧ T.IsAcyclic ∧
    ∃ develop : FacetPoint P → Plane,
      (∀ (F : Facet P) (x y : (F : Set Space)),
        dist (develop ⟨F, x⟩) (develop ⟨F, y⟩) = dist (x : Space) y) ∧
      (∀ p q, develop p = develop q ↔
        Relation.EqvGen (GluedAcrossUncutEdge P T) p q)

/--
Does every compact convex polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ have a net (equivalently, a simple
edge-unfolding)? Here the polyhedron is the boundary of the convex hull of finitely many points,
and nonempty interior excludes lower-dimensional degeneracies. The cuts must form a spanning
tree in the graph of actual polyhedral edges. The planar development is one-to-one, with even
incidental boundary touching disallowed.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem shephards_problem_a_k_a_durers_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ s : Set Space, s.Finite → (interior (convexHull ℝ s)).Nonempty →
      ∃ T : SimpleGraph (Vertex (convexHull ℝ s)),
        IsSimpleEdgeUnfolding (convexHull ℝ s) T := by
  sorry

end ShephardsProblemAKADurersConjecture
modeling_decisions: A convex polyhedron is represented as `convexHull ℝ s` for a finite set `s` in three-dimensional Euclidean space, with nonempty ambient interior to exclude lower-dimensional degeneracies. Finiteness makes this convex hull compact.
Actual facets and edges are represented as nonempty exposed faces whose affine spans have dimensions 2 and 1, respectively. This excludes pseudo-edges and face subdivisions.

Vertices are the extreme points of the convex hull. The cut graph has this full vertex type; requiring it to be connected and acyclic and to be a subgraph of the actual edge graph makes it a spanning tree of actual edges.

The cut surface is modeled using labelled copies of points in facets, modulo the equivalence relation generated by gluing copies across precisely the uncut actual edges. This handles the splitting of cut-edge interiors and vertices without introducing a separate polyhedral-surface topology library.

A planar development is required to preserve Euclidean distance within every facet. Equality of developed points is required to be equivalent to equality in the cut-surface quotient, expressing Ghomi's one-to-one isometric embedding convention.

Incidental boundary contacts are disallowed: two quotient-distinct points, including boundary points, cannot have the same planar image. This fixes the boundary-touching convention consistently and matches the cited primary source's use of a globally one-to-one unfolding.
Because the source is phrased as a yes/no question, the theorem uses `answer(sorry) ↔ ...` rather than asserting the conjectured positive answer directly.
